items.title: SI dimensionalization of the periodic diffuse-interface model
items.design_state: Necessary local A-page SI dimensionalization definition; draft authored and readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Use the dimensionless periodic torus $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$ with dimensionless coordinates $y\in\mathbb T^3$ and $s\in[0,S]$, where $S>0$. Its physical length-scale image is the periodic box $\Omega_L=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi L\mathbb Z)^3$, with physical coordinates $x=Ly$ and fundamental cube $Q_L=[0,2\pi L]^3$. Fields on $\Omega_L$ are represented by $(2\pi L\mathbb Z)^3$-periodic lifts, spatial derivatives are coordinate derivatives of these lifts, and spatial integrals mean Riemann integrals over $Q_L$. For a scalar field $g$, set $\nabla_xg=(\partial_{x_1}g,\partial_{x_2}g,\partial_{x_3}g)$ and $\Delta_xg=\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_{x_j}^2g$; for a vector field $u$, set $(\nabla_xu)_{ij}=\partial_{x_j}u_i$. Choose fixed scales $L>0$ in metres, $U>0$ in metres per second, $\rho_*>0$ in kilograms per cubic metre, and $\Phi_*>0$ in a specified phase unit $[\Phi]$. Set $T_*=L/U$, so physical time is $t=T_*s$ and the interval is $[0,T_*S]$.

Let $\varepsilon,M,\nu>0$ be dimensionless coefficients and let $W\in C^2(\mathbb R)$ be a dimensionless potential bounded below. For dimensionless fields $v(s,y)$, $\phi(s,y)$, and $\pi(s,y)$, define physical fields by

$$u(t,x)=U v(s,y),\qquad \varphi(t,x)=\Phi_*\phi(s,y),\qquad p(t,x)=\rho_*U^2\pi(s,y).$$

where $\mu_c=\varepsilon^{-1}W'(\phi)-\varepsilon\Delta_y\phi$. Define the positive physical coefficients

$$\beta=\frac{\rho_*U^2}{\varepsilon},\qquad \lambda_\phi=\frac{\rho_*U^2L^2\varepsilon}{\Phi_*^2},\qquad \eta=\rho_*UL\nu,\qquad \mathcal M=\frac{M\Phi_*^2L}{\rho_*U}.$$

Here $\beta$ is a bulk free-energy-density coefficient in joules per cubic metre, $\lambda_\phi$ is a gradient free-energy coefficient in joules per metre per phase-unit squared, $\eta$ is dynamic viscosity in pascal seconds, and $\mathcal M$ has units $[\Phi]^2\mathrm{m^3\,s\,kg^{-1}}$. The physical chemical potential has units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}[\Phi]^{-1}$ and the pressure has units pascals.

Define the bulk phase free-energy density, phase free-energy functional, and kinetic-plus-phase free-energy functional by

$$f_b(\varphi)=\beta W(\varphi/\Phi_*),\qquad \mathcal F[\varphi]=\int_{\Omega_L}\left(f_b(\varphi)+\frac{\lambda_\phi}{2}|\nabla_x\varphi|^2\right)\,dx,$$

$$\mathcal G[u,\varphi]=\int_{\Omega_L}\left(\frac{\rho_*}{2}|u|^2+f_b(\varphi)+\frac{\lambda_\phi}{2}|\nabla_x\varphi|^2\right)\,dx.$$

The dimensional chemical-potential field used by this model is

$$\mu=f_b'(\varphi)-\lambda_\phi\Delta_x\varphi=\frac{\beta}{\Phi_*}W'(\varphi/\Phi_*)-\lambda_\phi\Delta_x\varphi.$$

The length, speed, density, and phase scales are model inputs; no measured calibration is assigned by this definition.

references.title: J. Tinsley Oden, Lecture Notes, Fall 2016, Chapter 11: Phase-Field Models
V.E. Badalassi, H.D. Ceniceros, and S. Banerjee, Computation of multiphase systems with phase field models
references.locator: §§2.1–2.4, pp. 372–374, equations (1)–(15): free energy, chemical potential, convective Cahn–Hilliard equation, Model H coupling, and nondimensionalization.

items.physical_scope: SI scaling of the three-dimensional periodic, constant-density diffuse-interface model. The definition fixes length, time, density, phase, viscosity, mobility, free-energy, pressure, and chemical-potential units; it supplies no empirical calibration or claim of universal physical applicability.

items.title: Adopted diffuse free energy, mobility and capillary stress
items.design_state: Planned FD-PMP01 model adoption; draft authored and readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Adopt the following isothermal phase-field model in a Cartesian inertial chart with absolute time $t$ in seconds and spatial coordinates $x$ in metres. Let $L>0$ metres, $U>0$ metres per second, $\rho_*>0$ kilograms per cubic metre, and $\Phi_*>0$ in a chosen phase unit $[\Phi]$ be fixed scales. Let $S>0$, $T_*=L/U$, $\Omega_L=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi L\mathbb Z)^3$, and $t\in[0,T_*S]$. A physical field is represented by a $(2\pi L\mathbb Z)^3$-periodic function on $\mathbb R^3$, and its spatial integral is the Riemann integral over $Q_L=[0,2\pi L]^3$. Set $s=t/T_*$, $y=x/L$, $v=u/U$, $\phi=\varphi/\Phi_*$, and $\pi=p/(\rho_*U^2)$. The velocity is $u:[0,T_*S]\times\Omega_L\to\mathbb R^3$ in metres per second, the scalar order parameter is $\varphi:[0,T_*S]\times\Omega_L\to\mathbb R$ in phase units $[\Phi]$, and scalar pressure $p$ is in pascals. The order parameter is an internal phase variable, not total mass density; no positivity or pointwise interval constraint is imposed on it.

On $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$, require $v\in C^1([0,S];C^2_{\rm per}(\mathbb T^3;\mathbb R^3))$, $\phi\in C^1([0,S];C^1_{\rm per}(\mathbb T^3;\mathbb R))\cap C([0,S];C^2_{\rm per}(\mathbb T^3;\mathbb R))$, and $\pi\in C([0,S];C^1_{\rm per}(\mathbb T^3;\mathbb R))$, with $\mu_c=\varepsilon^{-1}W'(\phi)-\varepsilon\Delta_y\phi\in C([0,S];C^2_{\rm per})$. Here $C^k_{\rm per}$ means periodic lifts whose coordinate derivatives through order $k$ are continuous, bounded, and uniformly continuous on $[0,2\pi]^3$; time differentiability in $C^k_{\rm per}$ is in the corresponding supremum norms.

For a scalar field $g$, $\nabla_xg=(\partial_{x_1}g,\partial_{x_2}g,\partial_{x_3}g)$ and $\Delta_xg=\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_{x_j}^2g$; for a vector field $u$, $(\nabla_xu)_{ij}=\partial_{x_j}u_i$. On the dimensionless torus $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$, use periodic lifts and $\Delta_y=\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_{y_j}^2$. For the smooth branch, require $v\in C^1([0,S];C^2_{\rm per}(\mathbb T^3;\mathbb R^3))$, $\phi\in C^1([0,S];C^1_{\rm per}(\mathbb T^3;\mathbb R))\cap C([0,S];C^2_{\rm per}(\mathbb T^3;\mathbb R))$, and $\pi\in C([0,S];C^1_{\rm per}(\mathbb T^3;\mathbb R))$, with $\mu_c=\varepsilon^{-1}W'(\phi)-\varepsilon\Delta_y\phi\in C([0,S];C^2_{\rm per})$. Here $C^k_{\rm per}$ means periodic lifts whose coordinate derivatives through order $k$ are continuous, bounded, and uniformly continuous on the fundamental cube; time differentiability in $C^k_{\rm per}$ is in the corresponding supremum norms.

Use dimensionless parameters $\varepsilon,M,\nu>0$, a potential $W\in C^2(\mathbb R)$ bounded below, and the dimensional coefficients

$$\beta=\frac{\rho_*U^2}{\varepsilon},\qquad \lambda_\phi=\frac{\rho_*U^2L^2\varepsilon}{\Phi_*^2},\qquad \eta=\rho_*UL\nu,\qquad \mathcal M=\frac{M\Phi_*^2L}{\rho_*U}.$$

The bulk phase free-energy density is $f_b(\varphi)=\beta W(\varphi/\Phi_*)$ in joules per cubic metre. Define the chemical-potential field and the symmetric rate tensor by

$$\mu=f_b'(\varphi)-\lambda_\phi\Delta_x\varphi,\qquad D=\frac12\left(\nabla_xu+(\nabla_xu)^{\mathsf T}\right).$$

For vectors $a,b\in\mathbb R^3$, $(a\otimes b)_{ij}=a_i b_j$; $I_3$ is the $3\times3$ identity; and $(\operatorname{div}_x\sigma)_i=\sum_j\partial_{x_j}\sigma_{ij}$. Adopt the phase-field stress and total Cauchy stress

$$\sigma_c=\left(f_b(\varphi)-\varphi\mu+\frac{\lambda_\phi}{2}|\nabla_x\varphi|^2\right)I_3-\lambda_\phi\nabla_x\varphi\otimes\nabla_x\varphi,\qquad \sigma=-pI_3+2\eta D+\sigma_c,$$

where each stress has units pascals and traction is $\sigma n$ on an outward unit normal $n$. The adopted pointwise equations are

$$\partial_t\varphi+u\cdot\nabla_x\varphi=\mathcal M\Delta_x\mu,\qquad \nabla_x\cdot u=0,\qquad \rho_*\left(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla_x)u\right)=\operatorname{div}_x\sigma.$$

The model uses these smooth periodic fields, so its spatial integrals have no boundary terms. It adopts constant density, constant viscosity, constant mobility, and no external body force. The phase equation describes evolution of the internal order parameter and is not a total-mass diffusion equation. This is a reduced isothermal model: $\mathcal G=\int_{\Omega_L}(\rho_*|u|^2/2+f_b(\varphi)+\lambda_\phi|\nabla_x\varphi|^2/2)\,dx$ is kinetic plus phase-field free energy, not the complete thermodynamic energy. No heat or entropy balance, thermostat coupling, species-mass interpretation, sharp-interface limit, contact-line law, empirical calibration, or claim of universal physical validity is adopted.

items.physical_scope: An adopted isothermal, constant-density, incompressible phase-field model on a three-dimensional periodic box, with constant positive mobility and viscosity and a scalar internal order parameter. It does not identify that parameter with total mass density, assert an empirical calibration, supply a heat or entropy closure, or establish applicability to every two-phase material.

items.title: Conditional phase-field free-energy dissipation
items.design_state: Planned M1 conditional physical deduction; draft authored and readiness recorded separately.
items.statement:
Let $S,L,U,\rho_*,\Phi_*>0$ with units respectively dimensionless, metres, metres per second, kilograms per cubic metre, and a chosen phase unit $[\Phi]$. Put $T_*=L/U$, $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^3$, $\Omega_L=\mathbb R^3/(2\pi L\mathbb Z)^3$, and $t\in[0,T_*S]$. Fields on each torus are represented by periodic lifts and physical integrals are over $Q_L=[0,2\pi L]^3$. Let $\varepsilon,M,\nu>0$ be dimensionless and let $W\in C^2(\mathbb R)$ be bounded below. Define

$$\beta=\frac{\rho_*U^2}{\varepsilon},\qquad \lambda_\phi=\frac{\rho_*U^2L^2\varepsilon}{\Phi_*^2},\qquad \eta=\rho_*UL\nu,\qquad \mathcal M=\frac{M\Phi_*^2L}{\rho_*U},\qquad f_b(\varphi)=\beta W(\varphi/\Phi_*).$$

For periodic physical fields $u:[0,T_*S]\times\Omega_L\to\mathbb R^3$, $\varphi:[0,T_*S]\times\Omega_L\to\mathbb R$, and scalar pressure $p$, define

$$\mu=f_b'(\varphi)-\lambda_\phi\Delta_x\varphi,\qquad D=\frac12\left(\nabla_xu+(\nabla_xu)^{\mathsf T}\right),$$

$$\sigma=-pI_3+2\eta D+\left(f_b(\varphi)-\varphi\mu+\frac{\lambda_\phi}{2}|\nabla_x\varphi|^2\right)I_3-\lambda_\phi\nabla_x\varphi\otimes\nabla_x\varphi.$$

Assume the dimensionless fields $v(s,y)=u(T_*s,Ly)/U$, $\phi(s,y)=\varphi(T_*s,Ly)/\Phi_*$, and $\pi(s,y)=p(T_*s,Ly)/(\rho_*U^2)$ satisfy

$$v\in C^1([0,S];C^2_{\rm per}(\mathbb T^3;\mathbb R^3)),\qquad \phi\in C^1([0,S];C^1_{\rm per}(\mathbb T^3;\mathbb R))\cap C([0,S];C^2_{\rm per}(\mathbb T^3;\mathbb R)),\qquad \pi\in C([0,S];C^1_{\rm per}(\mathbb T^3;\mathbb R)),$$

with $\mu_c=\varepsilon^{-1}W'(\phi)-\varepsilon\Delta_y\phi\in C([0,S];C^2_{\rm per})$, and satisfy the adopted dimensional equations

$$\partial_t\varphi+u\cdot\nabla_x\varphi=\mathcal M\Delta_x\mu,\qquad \nabla_x\cdot u=0,\qquad \rho_*\left(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla_x)u\right)=\operatorname{div}_x\sigma,\quad (\operatorname{div}_x\sigma)_i=\sum_j\partial_{x_j}\sigma_{ij}.$$

Here $C^k_{\rm per}$ consists of periodic lifts whose coordinate derivatives through order $k$ are continuous, bounded, and uniformly continuous on $[0,2\pi]^3$; $C^1([0,S];C^k_{\rm per})$ means time differentiability in the corresponding supremum norms. For a scalar field $g$, $\nabla_xg=(\partial_{x_1}g,\partial_{x_2}g,\partial_{x_3}g)$ and $\Delta_xg=\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_{x_j}^2g$; for a vector field $u$, $(\nabla_xu)_{ij}=\partial_{x_j}u_i$.

For the kinetic-plus-phase free-energy functional

$$\mathcal G(t)=\int_{\Omega_L}\left(\frac{\rho_*}{2}|u(t,x)|^2+\frac{\lambda_\phi}{2}|\nabla_x\varphi(t,x)|^2+\beta W(\varphi(t,x)/\Phi_*)\right)\,dx,$$

where $|\nabla_xu|^2=\sum_{i,j=1}^3|\partial_{x_j}u_i|^2$, the conditional model identity is

$$\frac{d\mathcal G}{dt}(t)=-\eta\int_{\Omega_L}|\nabla_xu(t,x)|^2\,dx-\mathcal M\int_{\Omega_L}|\nabla_x\mu(t,x)|^2\,dx\qquad (0<t<T_*S).$$

The functional $\mathcal G$ is not the complete thermodynamic energy. This deduction neither asserts existence of such a solution nor derives the adopted isothermal closure from a total-energy or entropy balance.

This is not total thermodynamic energy, an existence theorem, an empirical conclusion, or a sharp-interface or immiscibility result.
